chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning...

About a man whom another man called while he was performing salat, so he became inattentive and answered him regarding his need—what should he do? He said: he continues with his salat and says takbīr many times.

So this does not contradict the first two reports regarding the obligation of the two sajdahs of forgetfulness upon him, because there is nothing in the report stating that the two sajdahs of forgetfulness are not upon him. Rather, he only commanded him to say takbīr, and it is not impossible that he should say takbīr as a recommended act and perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness as compensation.
As for speaking deliberately, it necessitates repeating the salat without disagreement, and that is not contradicted by this.

key_terms.تَكْبِيرًا: saying takbīr, the utterance of 'Allāhu akbar'
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in salat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone speaks forgetfully during salat, and does deliberate speech invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for one who speaks in salat forgetfully after responding to someone calling him. It indicates that he continues his salat and says takbīr frequently, while the compiler explains that this does not negate the obligation of the two sajdahs of forgetfulness; deliberate speech, however, requires repeating the salat.
